title: Software engineering work experience
titleCn: 软件工程专业实习经验

paragraphs.text: Part three.
You will hear a third-year student called Emma talking to a first-year student called John about the work experience John must do as part of his software engineering course.
First, you have some time to look at questions twenty-one to twenty-four.
Now listen carefully and answer questions twenty-one to twenty-four.
Hi, John. You wanted some advice about the work experience program?
Yeah. I wanted to check I've understood what I'm supposed to do.
Sure.
For a start, we have to work for a company in the holidays between the first and second year and again between the second and third year, right?
Yes. Usually, you do around fifty days with two different employers, like a hundred days in total.
I see. You know, there's one aspect of the work experience program I'm unhappy with. I mean, considering we have to attend a preparation course for it and that it's a big investment in terms of time.
What's the problem?
Just the fact that no matter how well we perform on the program, it makes no difference whatsoever to our final grade for our degree. It goes unrecognized.
I know, but there are lots of advantages too. Anyway, when does your preparation course for the work experience start?
Soon. We're starting with a session on interview technique, how to respond to questions, that stuff.
That can be useful. But I remember we had to make up a list of things we wanted to achieve during the time with the employer. That was a bit pointless.
My thoughts exactly. You can't decide on your aims until you've started work for real.
The tutor will give you some good advice about presenting your resume, though. So don't miss that session.
Okay. When the work experience starts for real, it would be great if I could actually do a bit of software design.

That's highly unlikely on a work experience course. You'll be doing more basic things than that. They might start you off on the IT help desk. That's often where they need extra people. But then you'll move on to work in areas that suit your field of study. I mean, whatever you focus on this year at college, you need to be able to put it into practice during work experience. There has to be a match.
And then we do work experience again after we finish our second year, right?
Mm-hmm.
I saw somewhere you can expect to earn between twenty to twenty-five dollars per hour. I suppose that's roughly what recent graduates get.
Yes, not bad.
But I also read employers don't necessarily have to pay you anything because you're not technically a real employee when you're doing work experience.
Uh, correct. But I haven't heard of that happening to anyone.
Unless you do IT work for some kind of volunteer organization.
I'd like to do that kind of thing, but not with my financial situation.
Right.
Before you hear the rest of the discussion, you have some time to look at questions twenty-five to thirty.
Now listen and answer questions twenty-five to thirty.

Okay. And once I've decided which company I want to do my work experience with, what's the process? Do I have to fill a form out first saying why I'd be interested to work for the company and what kind of qualifications I have?
Yes. You can ask your tutor for a standard one to use or download one off the department's website.
Okay. Then after that, do I have to sign something with the employer, like something that guarantees I'll be given the work over a specific period of time?
Actually, the next stage is you checking with the college that the kind of work you're applying for is appropriate. So you'll need to send them a brief outline of what your responsibilities will be.
All right.
And then, if the college approves, they'll speak to the company and get the name and email address of the managers that'll be in charge of you.
Okay. So after that, is there some kind of interview?
No. But the company are legally responsible for you, and they don't want you getting hurt by any equipment, so they'll set up a meeting.
So we can talk about accident prevention and that kind of thing.
Exactly. And once you've started, remember to keep writing down what you had to do every day. Be detailed, so you can show which skills you developed.
Right. And at what point might I receive a payment?

Mm, not sure. But once it's over, the college sends the employer a form, which they can choose to fill out or not, about how well you did and what they recommend you focus on next time. Do the tutors actually...
That is the end of part three. You now have thirty seconds to check your answers to Part three.
